# Nebius vs Thunder Compute (November 2026)

Nebius H100 NVLink is $4.50/hr; Thunder Compute H100 PCIe is $3.20/hr with per-minute billing. Compare GPU pricing, storage, and developer experience.

Carl Peterson · Updated Nov 04, 2026 · 7 min Read

Nebius is an AI-focused cloud backed by former Yandex engineers, with GPU infrastructure across Europe and the US. Thunder Compute focuses on low-cost, persistent GPU instances for individual developers and small teams.

This comparison covers GPU pricing, infrastructure, and developer experience for both providers.

Takeaways

- Nebius H100 NVLink on-demand: $4.50/hr.
- Thunder Compute H100 PCIe: $3.20/hr with per-minute billing.
- Nebius operates EU data centers with GDPR compliance. Thunder Compute operates in North America.
- Thunder Compute includes 100GB per GPU, one-click IDE extensions, and no egress fees.
- Nebius offers reserved capacity discounts up to 35% for multi-month commitments.

## What Thunder Compute Does

Thunder Compute takes a fundamentally different approach from enterprise-focused providers like Nebius. It's built for individual developers, researchers, and small teams who need powerful GPU computing without the complexity or cost of traditional cloud services.

Thunder Compute provides on-demand GPU instances with a focus on managed availability, low A100 pricing, persistent storage, and one-click IDE integration. A100 80GB starts at $1.09/hr and H100 PCIe at $3.20/hr, both billed per minute with no egress fees.

Thunder Compute provides on-demand GPU instances with 1-8 GPUs per machine, featuring NVIDIA options like A6000, L40, L40S, A100s, and H100. Cost optimization results from a software-driven approach that maximizes hardware performance, which passes savings directly to users.

Every instance includes 100GB per GPU at no extra charge. Your home directory and installed packages survive restarts automatically. Snapshots cost $0.05/GB/month and let you save and restore your full environment, including when switching GPU configurations.

results.title: Nebius raises GPU prices again October 1; H100 to $4.50, B300 to $9.50 | GPU Cloud Advisors
highlights:
Nebius raises GPU prices again October 1; H100 to $4.50, B300 to $9.50 | GPU Cloud Advisors

# Nebius raises GPU prices again October 1; H100 to $4.50, B300 to $9.50

Nebius lists higher on demand GPU prices effective October 1, 2026. H100 rises from $3.85 to $4.50 per GPU hour. H200 rises from $4.50 to $5.40, B200 from $7.15 to $8.50, and B300 from $7.85 to $9.50. This round is 17% to 21%. It is reported to be the second increase since May. [1] [2]

Published September 28, 2026 Announced, effective October 1, 2026

## Disclosed terms

HGX H100, per GPU hour

$3.85 now, $4.50 from October 1 [1]

HGX H200, per GPU hour

$4.50 now, $5.40 from October 1 [1]

HGX B200, per GPU hour

$7.15 now, $8.50 from October 1 [1]

HGX B300, per GPU hour

$7.85 now, $9.50 from October 1 [1]

## The disclosure and our analysis

### What changed

Nebius's pricing page now shows two on demand columns: today's rate and a rate effective October 1, 2026. H100 rises 17%, H200 20%, B200 19% and B300 21%. [1]

Spot rates still start at $0.79 for H100 and H200 and $0.99 for B200 and B300. RTX PRO 6000 stays at $1.80. CPU only instances also rise. Nebius still advertises commitment discounts of up to 35% off on demand for multi month cluster reservations. [1]

Nebius's pricing page does not give a reason for the change.

### The second increase this year

This is not the first increase. The Motley Fool reports that in early May, Nebius's pricing page showed H100 at $2.95 per hour and B300 at $6.10. [2] Our own catalog recorded H100 at $3.85 on September 18 and B300 at $7.85 on September 24.

If the May figures are right, the October rates are about 53% higher for H100 and 56% higher for B300 than five months earlier. [2] The trend matters more than any single rate. A budget built on spring pricing may already be out of date.

### How the new rates compare

We compared the new rates with published on demand rates in our provider catalog, checked September 18 to 28.

H100: At $4.50, Nebius moves above Runpod ($3.49), Crusoe ($3.90) and Lambda ($4.29). It stays below CoreWeave's 8 GPU instance, about $6.16 per GPU.

H200: At $5.40, Nebius moves above Runpod ($4.59) and Verda ($4.55). It stays below Together AI ($5.99) and CoreWeave (about $6.31 per GPU).

B200: At $8.50, Nebius moves well above Lambda ($6.69) and Runpod ($6.79). CoreWeave's 8 GPU instance works out to about $8.60 per GPU.

B300: At $9.50, Nebius moves above Verda ($8.20) and Scaleway ($7.50). Together AI lists $9.99.

Configurations differ. vCPUs, memory, storage, networking and minimum allocation all vary. A lower hourly rate is not a lower project cost on its own.

### What to do before October 1

Ask about locking today's rate. Ask Nebius whether a commitment signed before October 1 is priced at the current rate. Get the answer in writing, with the rate and term.

If you run on Nebius on demand today, your bill goes up October 1 unless your contract says otherwise. Check whether your agreement fixes the rate.

If you have a Nebius quote in hand, ask which rate it uses. A quote issued in September may still show the old price.

If you are planning a project, get a dated quote for your actual start date. Ask what a 3, 6 or 12 month commitment costs against the new on demand rate. Ask whether that commitment reserves GPUs or only lowers the rate.

If bookings hold at the new card, scarcity is confirmed and asset-backed finance gets cheaper to roll forward. If they flinch, the slowdown chorus gets its data point and the risk shifts from customers to lenders. One warning light I could not check: bears cite secondhand accelerator prices as the earliest signal of capex trouble, and no published index I could reach this week carries that number: the organized market for used GPUs↗ itself only opened on 17 July 10. That leaves the rate card as the cleanest public signal available.

When essays and price lists disagree, believe the price list, then verify it. Three markers after 1 October: on-demand utilization at the new rates, whether the next capacity auction again clears above the last, and whether Nebius funds its 2027 build from customer prepayments rather than another equity raise 7. The labs asked for time. The market is about to learn what an hour of it costs.

# Nebius to increase prices for Nvidia GPU resources from October

Editor Louis Juricic Stock Markets

Editor Louis Juricic

Published Sep 17, 2026, 09:47 AM

© Reuters

Investing.com -- Nebius will raise prices for its on-demand GPU services starting Oct. 1, the company said in an emailed statement, according to Bloomberg News. 

The price increases will apply to Nvidia H100, H200, B200 and B300 GPU resources, according to the statement. The company will also raise rates for certain CPU and memory resources.

The new pricing structure takes effect at the beginning of next month.
